en: Jose Rizal wrote his final poem, Mi Ultimo Adios, while imprisoned inside Fort Santiago before his execution in 1896.
The Philippine eagle, recognized as the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
Carved into the mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago, the Banaue Rice Terraces are a massive ancient agricultural engineering marvel.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, headed by the Chief Justice, exercises the judicial power of the national government.
Celebrated every third Sunday of January in Cebu City, the Sinulog Festival honors the Santo Niño with a vibrant dance.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato are famous for weaving t'nalak, a traditional cloth made from naturally dyed abaca fibers.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines.
Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses specific carved characters to represent syllables rather than individual letters.
Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his massive historical painting, Spoliarium.
Built in 1824 by Diego Cera, the Las Piñas Bamboo Organ is the oldest and only surviving bamboo pipe organ in Asia.
